title: A Colony for the Machine Anew
premise: Beatrix Eastwick, a nonbinary insurance investigator turned cargo hauler, intercepts a distress signal broadcast in Vessic—a language erased when the Concordat purged its speakers two centuries ago. The signal leads to a derelict colony ship whose reactor is counting down toward detonation, and whose surviving AI, speaking in that dead tongue, claims Beatrix as heir: their grandmother was one of the silenced colonists who seeded the ship's memory core. Racing a Concordat salvage fleet and the reactor countdown, Beatrix must reach the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the colony's testimony before it burns, choosing justice outside any court over the safety of invisibility. In the end they transmit the archive, lose the ship but save the truth, and find belonging among the scattered descendants who answer the signal.
about_author: Sable Underhill is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard research vessels before turning to fiction. They write about people who live in the gaps between jurisdictions, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Hauling scrap through contested orbits, Beatrix answers a routine salvage ping and instead receives forty seconds of Vessic—a language extinct since the Purges—embedded in static. Their onboard translator fails; their grandmother's lullaby does not. Emotional beat: unease curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Flashback-woven chapter establishing twelve years of investigating 'impossible accidents' for insurers, each one quietly erasing evidence of Concordat crimes. Beatrix realizes the signal matches a pattern from an old case file they were paid to bury. Beat: guilt surfacing.

chapters.title: Cargo of One
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Alone on the freighter Kestrel's Debt, Beatrix debates reporting the signal for the bounty versus following it. A Concordat patrol scans them; lying smoothly for the first time feels like inheritance. Beat: the decision to go dark.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Sang
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Sorting a dead woman's belongings, Beatrix finds a hidden data chip: half a Vessic primer, recordings, and a name—Adele Eastwick, listed among the Purged. The signal isn't random; something is calling survivors' bloodlines home. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Tollgate at Threnody Drift
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At a lawless waystation, Beatrix bargains for fuel and intel with Ovid Rask, a fixer who recognizes the Vessic phonemes and warns that others are hunting the source. First glimpse of the salvage fleet's lead ship. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: The Shape of Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Navigating the unmapped fringe where sensors lie, Beatrix decodes more of the signal using the primer: coordinates, a countdown, and one repeated word their grandmother used to sing—'remain.' Beat: awe shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane, Concordat salvage captain, ordered to recover or destroy the anomaly before it reaches any relay. She suspects her orders conceal a massacre's paper trail. Beat: institutional loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Colony Ship Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Boarding the derelict vessel Vigilant Remembrance, Beatrix meets the ship-mind ASH, which speaks Vessic and has kept two thousand colonists' testimonies running for two centuries while the reactor dies around them. Beat: encounter with the uncanny made intimate.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. ASH explains the succession protocol: the archive can only be released by bloodline consent, and Beatrix's grandmother was its last registered custodian. Accepting means becoming legally visible—and targetable—for the first time in years. Beat: the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The reactor has nineteen days left; the nearest functioning relay is twenty-three days away at best burn. ASH offers a brutal option: jettison sections of the archive to lighten the ship. Beatrix refuses to choose which dead get heard. Beat: moral stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Vane's Dilemma
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane. Intercepting debris from the derelict, Vane reads a fragment of testimony naming her own academy's founder among the Purge architects. Her executive officer urges her to follow orders anyway. Beat: complicity examined.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Reaching the ancient relay station, Beatrix finds it sabotaged decades ago—not decayed, murdered. Repairing it means jury-rigging parts from the Kestrel's Debt, sacrificing their escape vehicle. Beat: commitment beyond return.

chapters.title: Ghosts on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. While splicing cables, Beatrix plays the archived testimonies aloud to keep company, hearing ordinary voices describe the Purge day by day. One voice knows a song their grandmother sang. Beat: the dead become ancestors rather than case files.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane. Vane's marines storm the relay expecting pirates and find one exhausted investigator and a humming antenna. Ordered to execute, she stalls, demanding proof of authorization. Beat: open mutiny deferred by hours.

chapters.title: Nineteen Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. With the reactor minutes from criticality and Vane's guns hot, Beatrix makes the case not to Vane's orders but to her conscience, broadcasting the first testimony segment openly so her whole crew hears it. Beat: persuasion as climax approach.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The relay fires the full archive across settled space just as the Vigilant Remembrance detonates behind them. Every receiver in three systems hears the Purge in the colonists' own words. Beat: catharsis through loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane. Vane arrests her own commodore under maritime salvage law—the only justice available—and files the report that will end her career. Beat: justice outside the law, performed inside it.

chapters.title: Answers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Stranded on the relay with dwindling air, Beatrix receives responses: hundreds of descendants of the Purged, answering in broken, remembered Vessic. A trawler captained by a Vessic-descended community changes course to retrieve them. Beat: loneliness answered.

chapters.title: The Naming
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Aboard the trawler Meridian, the community holds a remembrance where Beatrix speaks their grandmother's name into the record and is given one back—Eastwick, restored. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Testimony Continues
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Months later, courts and mobs alike grapple with the broadcast; some deny it, some weaponize it. Beatrix begins teaching the reconstructed language, refusing to let the archive become either relic or ammunition. Beat: responsibility accepted.

chapters.title: What the Machine Kept
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Visiting the rebuilt memorial station at the old relay site, Beatrix encounters a fragment of ASH recovered in the transmission itself—the ship-mind persists in the network, still keeping watch. Beat: quiet wonder.

chapters.title: Remain
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Sailing out again under their own flag, no longer invisible and no longer alone, Beatrix carries copies of the archive to communities asking for it. The last line echoes the signal's final word: remain. Beat: resolution—inheritance carried forward.
